body.text: Understanding how the [Turkish Revenue Administration (GİB)](https://gib.gov.tr/) taxes resale gains, annual assessments, and succession prevents costly surprises after closing. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about)—an independent, client-paid, flat-fee travel advisory run by its two founders in Türkiye ("Paid by our clients. Independent of provider commissions.")—we coordinate visit logistics and independent introductions, while licensed Turkish professionals provide all tax and legal advice.
When does Türkiye's 5-year capital gains tax exemption apply on resale?

Under Turkish Income Tax Law, an individual who holds a purchased property for more than five full years from the title deed registration date pays zero Turkish capital gains tax on resale, regardless of nationality. Selling within five years triggers progressive income tax (15%–40%) on the inflation-adjusted net gain above the annual exemption.

Per [GİB's Other Gains guide](https://www.gib.gov.tr/vergi-konulari/1_bireysel/7_diger_kazanc_ve_iratlar/7), the five-year clock runs to the exact day from Tapu registration (or kat irtifakı registration). Inherited or gifted properties are excluded even if sold earlier. On resales within five years, purchase cost is indexed by Yİ-ÜFE whenever cumulative inflation reaches 10%, and the first 150,000 TL of 2026 net gain is exempt.
How much is annual municipal property tax (Emlak Vergisi)?

Annual municipal property tax (Emlak Vergisi) is calculated on the municipality's assessed tax value (rayiç bedel), not the market purchase price. In Türkiye's 30 metropolitan municipalities—including Istanbul, İzmir, Muğla (Bodrum), and Antalya—residential property is taxed at 0.2% per year and commercial property at 0.4%, while non-metropolitan provinces charge half those rates.

body.text: Homes assessed above 17,711,000 TL in 2026 also face Luxury Housing Tax (Değerli Konut Vergisi) per [BestHome's 2026 overview](https://besthome.com.tr/en/blog-vlog/blog/taxes/taxes-in-turkiye-for-foreign-nationals-in-2026/), unless exempt as a single residence. Taxes are paid via local municipalities or the [GİB Digital Tax Office](https://dijital.gib.gov.tr/).
How do Turkish inheritance rules apply to foreign-owned real estate?

Immovable property located in Türkiye is governed by Turkish inheritance law and Turkish inheritance tax (Veraset ve İntikal Vergisi), regardless of the owner's citizenship or where they live. Heirs must obtain a Turkish Certificate of Inheritance (veraset ilamı) and file a tax declaration before the Land Registry transfers the title deed.

Per [GİB's 2026 inheritance schedule](https://www.gib.gov.tr/vergi-konulari/1_bireysel/12_veraset_ve_intikal_vergisi/12), the tax-free allowance is 2,907,136 TL per child or spouse (5,817,845 TL if the spouse is sole heir). Excess value is taxed at 1%–10% across six installments over three years. Filing is mandatory even below the threshold, and many foreign owners execute a Turkish-compliant will to navigate forced-heirship rules.
Why should buyers consult a licensed tax advisor (SMMM) before closing?

A licensed Turkish Certified Public Accountant (Serbest Muhasebeci Mali Müşavir, or SMMM) verifies your tax identification number, reviews title-deed declared value against banking transfers, and models residency, rental, and double-taxation treaty impacts before you sign. Fixing an under-declared deed or missed filing after closing is far more expensive than getting it right upfront.
Run through this pre-closing checklist with independent advisors:

items: Verify your SMMM's active license via [TÜRMOB](https://www.turmob.org.tr/English).
Compare personal vs. corporate ownership (companies lose the individual 5-year capital gains exemption).
Check double-taxation treaties between your home country and Türkiye.
Match declared Tapu value to bank transfers to avoid inflated future gains.
Have a Turkish attorney review forced-heirship rules and local will options.

faq.q: Do foreign nationals qualify for the 5-year capital gains exemption?
faq.a: Yes. Individual owners qualify regardless of citizenship, provided the property is not a business asset and is held past five full years from Tapu registration.

faq.q: Does the 3-year citizenship hold exempt me from capital gains tax?
faq.a: No. The three-year citizenship hold is an immigration rule; selling in year four still triggers capital gains tax unless you pass year five.

faq.q: How do non-resident owners pay annual Emlak Vergisi?
faq.a: Pay in May and November via municipal e-Belediye portals using your Turkish tax number, or through an authorized SMMM.

faq.q: Does a foreign will automatically govern Turkish real estate?
faq.a: No. Turkish immovable property follows Turkish succession law, so attorneys commonly advise drafting a parallel Turkish will.

faq.q: What is the 2026 capital gains exemption on sales under five years?
faq.a: For 2026 sales, [GİB](https://www.gib.gov.tr/vergi-konulari/1_bireysel/7_diger_kazanc_ve_iratlar/7) sets the annual exemption (istisna) at 150,000 TL on inflation-adjusted net gain.
